newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Index rises in brisk Nigerian share trade.
newsitem.headline: Index rises in brisk Nigerian share trade.

text.p: Buoyed by oil marketing company shares, the Nigerian stock market index rose in brisk trade on Monday, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 6,789.61 from 6,775.61 on Friday.
As well as the oil companies, breweries ended strongly as did food and beverage companies and some bank shares.
Total and Texaco were 50 kobo higher at 54.50 naira and 31.00 naira respectively. Unipetrol was 40 kobo up at 52.40 naira and Agip ended 35 kobo higher at 19.10 naira.
Nestle continued to impress traders, rising 40 kobo to 45.60 naira, while Union Dicon Salt climbed 15 kobo to 42.03 naira.
Cadbury was the big faller among food companies, closing 40 kobo lower at 24.30 naira.
Traders said there was no end in sight to large scale dumping of the shares.
For the same reason, Lever Brothers fell 30 kobo to 22.00 naira and fellow conglomerate CFAO dropped seven kobo to end at 3.50 naira.
Ashaka Cement too joined the fallers, down 10 kobo to 18.35 naira, on investors' fears that poor sales reports would reduce profits.
But such fears were not entertained in respect of sector leader West African Portland Cement Company which rose 30 kobo to 41.30 naira.
United Bank for Africa was the best finisher in its sector, going 10 kobo up at 5.40 naira. FSB International Bank closed five kobo higher at 5.40 naira.
Union Bank and Afribank slipped by five kobo each to 5.75 naira and 4.70 naira respectively.
Cheering third quarter results from packaging company Delta Glass earned it a 15 kobo rise to 6.65 naira.
